name: abb-python
description: Write Python code for ABB robots with the UnderAutomation ABB SDK.

interface.longDescription:
UnderAutomation ABB SDK for Python (pip UnderAutomation.ABB, import underautomation.abb). Use it when Python code talks to an ABB robot controller (IRC5 with RobotWare 6, OmniCore with RobotWare 7) or a RobotStudio virtual controller, or when the user asks about the ABB SDK, Robot Web Services or its exceptions. Protocol of the SDK: Robot Web Services (RWS 1.0 on IRC5, RWS 2.0 on OmniCore), plus the discovery of the controllers of the network. It answers questions such as which RWS version and which mastership domain to use, how to read and write RAPID variables and I/O signals, how to start and stop a RAPID program, read the robot position, jog the robot, compute the kinematics, manage files, backups and the event log, and why an RwsException is raised. It holds the documentation pages, the Python code samples and the list of every public class and member of the package, with the Python names.

Intended users: developers who write Python applications that connect a PC to a ABB robot controller with the UnderAutomation ABB SDK.

Limitations: the skill is documentation only. It does not connect to the robot and does not run code by itself. It documents version 1.1.0 of the SDK. The SDK (pip UnderAutomation.ABB) must be installed in the project and has its own license agreement.
capabilities: Choose the protocol and the controller option for a task
Write Python code with the public API of the ABB SDK 1.1.0
Explain the exceptions of the SDK and what to check
Apply safety rules to the code that moves a robot
defaultPrompt: What do I need on my OmniCore controller to write a RAPID variable from my application?
Write a program that reads the robot position and the digital inputs of my ABB robot.
Why do I get an RwsException with HTTP 403 when I write a RAPID variable?
